tagline: AI paraphrasing, summarizing, and grammar checking.
verdictSummary: A paraphrase-and-grammar tool wrapping an LLM plus a local grammar engine is a one-sitting build — QuillBot's actual value is almost entirely wrapper polish (browser and Word extensions, saved history, purpose-built modes), not a capability that's hard to reproduce.
coreLoopDIY: A page with an input and output pane: paraphrase and summarize through an LLM, grammar-check through a local open-source engine, with every run saved to a searchable history.
whatYouLose: browser and Word extensions that work inline where you're already writing
years of UX polish on rewrite modes
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because it's already installed where they write, with purpose-built buttons for each mode — not because paraphrasing text is a hard problem to solve.
notes: A strong yes: this is wrapper-heavy in exactly the way that makes cancellation easy once the DIY version exists.
prompt:
Build a small local tool with one text box in, one output pane, and buttons for a few fixed modes: paraphrase, summarize, and a couple of tone rewrites (more formal, shorter). Paraphrase, summarize, and tone modes call an LLM API with a fixed instruction per mode and stream the response. Grammar checking runs through a local open-source grammar engine (LanguageTool, self-hosted) rather than the LLM — grammar is a solved problem and shouldn't cost API tokens. Show a word-level diff between input and output so a rewrite's changes are visible at a glance. Save every run (mode, input, output, timestamp) to a database with a history view you can copy back out of.

Do not build browser or word-processor extensions, or plagiarism/AI-detection features — those need real platform integration work and separate detection models respectively, and neither is what makes the core paraphrase-and-grammar loop useful. This lives in one tab, and that's the honest trade against a tool that's installed everywhere you type.

faq.q: Can I import my QuillBot history?
faq.a: No — QuillBot doesn't offer an export of your saved rewrite history, so past work stays there. Everything from this build forward is saved locally in your own database.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a page with a text box, yes, technically — but there's no browser extension or Word integration, so on mobile specifically you'd be copying text in and out manually, which is a real downgrade.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting for the small server plus LLM API usage per paraphrase or summary call — grammar checking itself is free, since it runs on a local open-source engine with no API cost.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Being where you already write. QuillBot's extensions work inline in your browser or Word; this build is a separate tab you copy text into and out of, every time.
